article_title: DeepSeek Open-Sources Harness Agent Framework Under MIT License, Ships V4-Pro With Native Responses API Support
summary: Well-sourced and substantively accurate across all 4 sources, but one quote does not match TechNode's exact wording.

findings.message: The article quotes TechNode as "positioning it as an open-source alternative to Anthropic's Claude Cowork." TechNode's actual wording is: "an open-source agent harness positioned against Anthropic's Claude Cowork." The meaning is preserved but the wording inside the quote marks is paraphrased, not verbatim.

content_preview.title: DeepSeek Open-Sources Harness Agent Framework Under MIT License, Ships V4-Pro With Native Responses API Support
content_preview.summary: DeepSeek released its Harness agent runtime as MIT-licensed open source and rolled out DeepSeek-V4-Pro with native OpenAI Responses API support.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

DeepSeek has released DeepSeek Harness, an open-source agent runtime framework, as a developer preview under the MIT license, according to the project's [GitHub repository](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). The release came alongside an API update to DeepSeek-V4-Pro that adds native support for the OpenAI Responses API format, as reported by [TechNode](https://technode.com/2026/08/13/deepseek-v4-pro-api-update-adds-responses-api-support/).

editor_notes.content_quality: Concise, well-organized News piece covering two related DeepSeek announcements (Harness open-sourcing and V4-Pro API update) with appropriate weight given to each.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 4 snapshots directly, plus one live check for a claim the snapshot couldn't verify. The GitHub repo page (source-0) confirms the 'Everything is a Plugin' tagline and the 86.2k stars / 7.6k forks figures (article's 'more than 85,000' / 'over 7,500' framing is an accurate conservative rounding). The raw README (source-1) confirms the plugin-architecture description, the Cordis attribution, the developer-preview warning (including the bolded all-caps compatibility-breaking-changes line), the dsh command, and the MIT license verbatim. The specific '0.1.0-rc.5' version claim could not be verified from the GitHub landing-page snapshot (package.json contents aren't rendered on that page) -- independently confirmed via a direct fetch of the raw package.json, which shows version 0.1.0-rc.5 exactly as claimed. TechNode's Harness article (source-2) confirms the web-interface, Cordis-architecture, and compatibility-breaking-changes claims verbatim, but the 'positioning it as an open-source alternative' quote is a paraphrase of the source's actual 'positioned against' wording (see finding). TechNode's V4-Pro article (source-3) confirms every technical spec and all three pricing figures verbatim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics verify against their cited sources, including one that required an independent live check beyond the saved snapshot. Only the one quote-fidelity issue found.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate -- the only prior DeepSeek-adjacent archive article covers the earlier V4 base model launch, a distinct product.
concerns: One quote ("positioning it as an open-source alternative to Anthropic's Claude Cowork") paraphrases rather than reproduces TechNode's wording exactly -- see the filed corrections record.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Approve with corrections. The article is accurate and well-sourced; the single quote-fidelity issue is minor, isolated to a subordinate claim, and is honestly covered by a public corrections note.
